claims.statement: scripts/infra-image-scan.mjs partitions images by COVERAGE rather than namespace: an image is scanned by whoever builds it, and everything else is enumerated here. The exclusion is membership of BUILT_IMAGE_NAMES — exactly the six cd-deploy app images, since feature 080 deleted the only other builder — not a `jumbleknot/` prefix test, so the invariant is exactly one scanner per image, not zero and not two; the guard asserts the list is exactly those six and asserts completeness against a hypothetical fixture in scripts/__tests__/infra-image-scan.test.mjs.

A `image:` ref whose registry host is the interpolated `${REGISTRY_HOST}` (the only way a committed file may name an image this project publishes, because check-topology-scrub forbids the forge host) is resolved and enumerated when the variable is set; when it is unset on a real scan the orchestrator EXITS 2 rather than skipping quietly, because a sweep that silently covers fewer images and still passes is worse than one that fails loudly. The workflow no longer supplies REGISTRY_HOST at all (feature 080 removed its only consumer), so today no compose ref depends on it — but a ref that later needs it makes the scan exit 2 naming the ref instead of shrinking coverage, and cd-deploy's own `${REGISTRY_HOST}/…@${DIGEST}` refs are deliberately not reported as unresolved since they are excluded for two other reasons.

The infra-image gate blocks only a FIXABLE Critical: normalizeTrivy marks `blocking = severity === 'Critical' && a FixedVersion exists`, matching the sibling cd-deploy Trivy gate's `--severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`; unfixable Criticals and all fixable High/Medium/Low findings are report-only warnings, and the gate consumes the report's `blocking` flag rather than re-deriving the criterion.

The scan and the verdict are two commands so that one exit code carries one meaning: scripts/infra-image-scan.mjs runs Trivy with --format json and no --exit-code (non-zero therefore means only that the scanner could not run), and scripts/check-infra-image-findings.mjs carries the vulnerability verdict from the normalized report. scripts/cd/scan-app-image.sh is the single per-image contract that wires the pair together, mapping a failed scan to exit 10 and a failed gate to exit 11 (0 clean, 2 usage), and it is the ONLY place the two commands run: cd-deploy's scan-push.sh calls it before each `docker push`, and app-ci's `app-image-scan` job calls it on the six images `app-e2e` built, so the PR and the deploy share one Trivy pin, one set of flags and one allowlist — and an accepted finding lives in security/infra-images/allowlist.yaml instead of a .trivyignore nobody reviews.

scanImage() invokes Trivy through the shared bounded-retry driver in scripts/lib/scanner-retry.mjs (three attempts, exponential 2s/4s backoff), preserving fail-closed behaviour and retrying only a narrowly-classified transport/service failure; the classifier is handed STDERR only, because Trivy writes the vulnerability report to stdout and classifying stdout would let an advisory title decide whether a scan is retried, and the captured stderr in the failure message is the TAIL (readTail) rather than the head.

The authoritative sweep runs on a twice-weekly schedule (Tuesday and Friday 04:00 UTC) and is not path-gated, while the pull_request trigger deliberately has no `paths:` filter so the required `infra-image-scan / infra-image-scan` context is always posted; the Trivy steps are gated by an always-running `changes` job and a RUN_SCAN expression that forces the full sweep on every non-pull_request event.

scripts/publish-sweep-verdict.mjs posts an `infra-image-scan/weekly` commit status derived from the gate's, scan's and job's measured outcomes — distinguishing blocking CVEs from a sweep that could not run, publishing nothing for a cancelled run — and the context deliberately has no ` / ` separator so it cannot match branch protection's `infra-image-scan / infra-image-scan*` glob and cannot gate a merge.

The allowlist expiry check runs only on scheduled runs, guarded by `always() && github.event_name == 'schedule'` so a red CVE gate cannot skip it while a dated entry can never block a pull request, and the job publishes the measured `event_name`, `gate` and `expiry_step` values as an always-`success` `infra-image-scan/expiry` commit status so that a step that ran and one that skipped are distinguishable without logs.

An allowlist entry suppresses a finding only when its `image` regex (matched unanchored against the full scanned repo:tag) and its `id` regex both match and its `expiry` is absent or not past; image/id/justification/addedBy are all required, a blank field or invalid regex is a gate error, and suppression is gate-only — allowlisted findings stay visible in the report.

Suppressions must be dischargeable by an upgrade: scripts/__tests__/infra-image-scan.test.mjs asserts for every formerly-floating repository that each allowlist key still matches the reference in the compose files today AND stops matching a synthetic later version, derived by incrementing the last numeric component of the actual pin (with a self-check that the derived ref differs from the pin) rather than read from a hand-written 'next version' map that a bump can silently invalidate; a tag with no number fails loudly and asks for a declared exception rather than passing vacuously.

Unmatched-allowlist-entry detection is scoped to the images a run actually scanned (`generatedForImages`, required rather than defaulted), because two jobs consult the same infra-image allowlist — the full sweep and cd-deploy's single-image scan-push loop, whose findings both carry the literal scanner `trivy` — and each otherwise reported the other's live entries as suppressing nothing.

The floating-tag exception set is asserted as SET EQUALITY between the references the scanner classifies as floating in infrastructure-as-code/** and the declared exceptions read from renovate.json's docker-datasource `regex:^RELEASE` versioning rules; the set is empty because the date-tagged images left the tree (feature 069) and their from-source successor left with feature 080 — not because the classifier was weakened — and the anti-widening protection lives in tests (fd1)-(fd4) that assert isFloatingTag's behaviour directly instead of in a non-zero count.

The `dorny/paths-filter` step in `infra-image-scan.yml`'s `changes` job is gated on `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` because dorny derives its diff base from the PR event and otherwise falls back to the repository default branch, which this forge does not put in the payload, so the action hard-errors. That error killed `changes` on the cron, and since the required `infra-image-scan` job is `needs: [changes]` the full sweep was silently skipped; when the filter step is skipped its output is empty and `RUN_SCAN`'s `github.event_name != 'pull_request'` clause forces the sweep, which is the intended behaviour.

scripts/infra-image-scan.mjs uses deliberate exit codes — 0 ok, 1 scan/gate-relevant failure (fail-closed), 2 bad args or config error — and offers `--image <ref>` to scan exactly one image instead of enumerating the tree (the mode a builder uses to scan its own artifact), `--list` to enumerate without Trivy, and `--emit-allowlist` to write a proposed baseline. Severity normalization is data-driven: `loadSeverityMap()` throws on an unmapped native Trivy severity (no silent default) and `UNKNOWN` maps conservatively to `Low` so it can never block.

`--check-expiring` in scripts/check-infra-image-findings.mjs is report-only: it skips the blocking-finding gate entirely and fails on allowlist hygiene alone (an entry expiring within 14 days, already expired, or matching nothing), so the weekly step can never fail for a reason the gate above already owns and cannot turn a red gate green. The gate also ships a `--selftest` that CI runs before the real scan, so a broken gate is not mistaken for a clean sweep.

The keyless constraint is why an image's own builder scans it rather than routing it to this sweep: no credential reaches the scan (Trivy runs with no registry auth and is handed no secret), while our built images live in a private registry, so Trivy here cannot pull them (measured: `unable to find the specified image`). The workflow's only secret reference is `CI_DIGEST_TOKEN`, consumed by the feature-042 failure-digest step and never by the scan, so the keyless property holds even though the workflow does interpolate a secret. A builder already holds the image locally and is already authenticated, so it needs no new credential and gates the publish instead of auditing after it.

The `infra-image-scan/expiry` status cannot separate the two causes of `expiry_step=failure`: an allowlist entry needing action (expiring within 14 days, already expired, or matching nothing), or the checker itself crashing — item #562, where from 2026-09-12 until 2026-10-02 both checkers threw on the absent report they announce as legitimate and, because the step runs `cmd1 && cmd2` under `bash -e`, the infra-image half never ran at all. A `GateError` stack trace in the step log is the tell for the second cause.

The ordering of the infra-image sweep ahead of the Renovate window is enforced by a guard test rather than by a comment: `scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` asserts that the latest `infra-image-scan.yml` cron fires strictly earlier than the earliest `renovate.yml` window cron, with a gap of at least two hours to absorb queue depth (the sweep itself takes ~3 minutes but the capacity-1 runner may be inside a ~35-minute app-e2e, and a heavy weekly image build sits between them), and that both crons are UTC-fixed 5-field expressions so DST cannot narrow the gap (item #487).

The Tuesday 04:00 UTC cron was added (item #642) because a Friday-only sweep leaves only three hours to triage: GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j against the unchanged `langfuse:4` pins was published 2026-09-22, was absent from Trivy's DB for the 2026-09-25 sweep, and first surfaced at 04:00 on 2026-10-02, so the window's PRs and every other PR inherited a red nobody had seen. Tuesday 04:00 is hour-of-week 52, far ahead of the window, so the item #487 ordering guard still compares against Friday 04:00.

The declared floating-tag exception set is read from renovate.json rules matching the DOCKER datasource specifically, because that list means "image references whose tag the classifier cannot order". Feature 069 added a date-versioning rule on the `github-releases` datasource tracking the source release compiled into our own image, which was deliberately excluded from the declaration; feature 080 deleted that rule with the build, so the declaration and the exception set are both legitimately empty.

`${REGISTRY_HOST}` in an `image:` ref is resolved by a REGEX rather than a literal match, so the guarded compose form `${REGISTRY_HOST:?set in …}` — which contains spaces — resolves; a literal match silently stopped resolving the moment a ref was brought into line with that convention, and the failure presented as "the substitution does nothing" rather than as a parse error.

Feature 080 replaced the from-source object store with an upstream digest-pinned `rustfs/rustfs` Docker Hub pull, so RustFS is enumerated by this sweep like every other third-party server image, in every compose file that pins it; a guard test asserts the real tree carries exactly ONE digest-pinned `rustfs/rustfs` ref across at least six locations, which is the coverage property that replaced the retired build's self-scan.

`scripts/__tests__/no-minio-references.guard.test.mjs` fails the build on any live reference to the retired object store — matching every tracked file's path and content case-insensitively — with a CLOSED list of reasoned path/line/token exemptions and with history blocks permitted only under `docs/runbooks/**` between explicit begin/end markers; an exemption that matches nothing fails, the same rule the allowlist gate applies to an unmatched entry.

cd-deploy keeps scanning/gating a push distinct from promoting the resulting digests: scripts/cd/scan-push.sh scans each built image with the shared pipeline and blocks the push on an un-allowlisted fixable Critical, while scripts/cd/promote-digest.sh is a separate step that writes the resulting bare digests into the tracked .env.deploy files (as a commit carrying `[skip ci]`).

The transferred lesson 'publishing is not promoting' is recorded in the source runbook: PR #559 bumped the builder base image as a security bump, the workflow rebuilt and published the image, and every compose ref still pinned the pre-#559 digest three weeks later (item #577), so a scan of an artifact as built says nothing about the image as deployed until a promotion repoints the pins — and on a registry that drops an untagged manifest, a build must also be pushed under an immutable per-run tag or a rebuild orphans the digest the refs pin.

The transferred lesson 'a count of refs to repoint comes from the tree, never from a note' is recorded in the source runbook: a spec note recording four refs went stale when a later feature added two more, so the promoter's replacement scans the tree on every run and treats an empty result as a hard failure, because a promoter that silently matches zero refs is indistinguishable from one that worked.

The transferred lesson 'choosing a tool to avoid a decision removes your control of the decision' is recorded in the source runbook: resolving a published digest via `docker buildx imagetools inspect` failed over plain HTTP while `docker push` succeeded in the same job, because imagetools is a client-side operation that ignores the daemon's `insecure-registries` configuration — so a digest is resolved by asking the registry directly for the manifest LIST, and the scheme is taken from an explicit setting or the forge origin and fails rather than defaulting to https.

The transferred lesson 'a rule is not an update channel — extraction is' is recorded in docs/runbooks/renovate.md (item #560) and restated in renovate.json's `rustfs/rustfs` rule description, and reinforced by a guard here: a Renovate `packageRule` can resolve, and a rule-level guard can pass, while nothing extracts the dependency it describes, so the per-file counts under the Dependency Dashboard's Detected Dependencies are the only statement of what was actually extracted; `scripts/__tests__/infra-image-scan.test.mjs`'s `(412)` test asserts VISIBILITY (every compose file carrying an `image:` matches a docker-compose managerFilePattern, with `docs/proposals/**` excluded via `ignorePaths`) rather than configuration.

The cron-ordering guard also asserts the REASON is written down where the next editor will see it: `renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` fails unless `.forgejo/workflows/infra-image-scan.yml` still contains an `item #487` reference explaining why its cron sits at 04:00, on the reasoning that an unexplained time is the one a later reader tidies away.

The Trivy install in `.forgejo/workflows/infra-image-scan.yml`, `cd-deploy.yml` and `app-ci.yml` is version-pinned rather than floating: each file writes the version ONCE as a `TRIVY_VERSION=vX.Y.Z` assignment and hands it to `scripts/ci-install-trivy.sh <vX.Y.Z> <bindir>`, so a bump cannot move one site and strand the other. There are three such sites since spec 084 US3 (app-ci's `app-image-scan` must scan the PR's images with the scanner the deploy will use, or a green PR says nothing about the deploy). `scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` asserts the RESOLVED state across all three files — each resolving to a `vX.Y.Z` tag, all three agreeing on one version (a disagreement means one gate can block what another passes), none of them piping the vendor's `contrib/install.sh` or reaching `get.trivy.dev` again — and that the `aquasecurity/trivy` customManager (datasource `github-releases`) covers all three files and actually captures a `currentValue` in each, since a manager whose regex misses is indistinguishable from no manager at all.

Renovate visibility of the object store is asserted twice at two scopes: `scripts/__tests__/infra-image-scan.test.mjs`'s `(412)` test covers every compose file carrying an `image:` against the docker-compose `managerFilePattern`s (plus the `ignorePaths` exclusion for `docs/proposals/**`), while `scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs`'s `(080b)` test adds the RustFS-specific case — deriving the file set from `git ls-files` rather than a hand-written list and requiring each file pinning `rustfs/rustfs` to match a `docker-compose` pattern and not be ignored — so a later compose file in an unmatched directory fails the build instead of silently joining the set nothing proposes updates for.

The item #487 cron-ordering guard selects the Renovate WINDOW cron STRUCTURALLY rather than by name: it keeps only the `renovate.yml` schedule entries that fire exactly one hour-of-week slot, so the nightly `0 3 * * *` (seven slots, the schedule-exempt security channel) drops out and the single-slot Friday window cron is what the sweep is ordered against; the guard also fails loudly if no single-slot cron remains. Adding another single-slot cron to `renovate.yml` therefore moves what the ordering is asserted against rather than passing vacuously.

Where a reference is a floating major, or the advisory survives a version move, the allowlist entry is keyed to the DIGEST so that an upstream rebuild — not a tag move — is what discharges it: the OpenSearch entry is `opensearchproject/opensearch:3@sha256:bcc17975…` rather than `opensearch:3` and was re-keyed from the 2.x digest to the 3.x one when the OpenSearch 3 major did NOT clear CVE-2026-75595. The Unleash entry named version AND digest (`^unleashorg/unleash-server:8\.2\.1@sha256:c6eaaede7242`) so any image change re-blocked: it was re-keyed 8.2.0 → 8.2.1 in the 2026-10-30 Renovate window after the new digest was re-measured and still carried proxy-addr 2.0.7 under the boolean `trust proxy` that keeps CVE-2026-90711 unreachable, and it was then DISCHARGED on 2026-11-01 rather than re-keyed again, because the 8.3.1 rebuild (`sha256:025cd8b003a7`, the digest every unleash ref now pins) ships proxy-addr 2.0.8 as the only copy in the image and was scanned at zero fixable Criticals.

The `hashicorp/vault` security hold is discharged and replaced by an approval gate: the renovate.json `allowedVersions` ceiling below 1.19 stood from 2026-08-30 to 2026-10-20, was lifted by feature 081 US8c after `vault:2.2.0@sha256:e0acd3c6…` measured ZERO Criticals of any kind, both vault refs moved to the digest-pinned 2.x line, and the three `hashicorp/vault:1\.18` seed entries were DELETED rather than re-keyed (a re-keyed entry would match nothing and fail the expiry check). With no vault entry allowlisted, the infra-image scan itself is now the hold — it blocks any fixable Critical in a proposed vault tag — while a vault MAJOR (raft storage on a dormant prod stack) requires a dependency-dashboard tick and patch/minor stay automatic and scan-gated.

The infra-image allowlist holds six live entries (measured 2026-11-01) in three shapes. Two are the un-expiring BASELINE for the same Go-stdlib Critical CVE-2025-68121 on `postgres:18\.6-alpine3\.23` and `postgres:18-alpine`, each recording its own measurement because no reachable tag clears it (the shipped binary carrying it is `usr/local/bin/gosu`). The other four are time-boxed to `2026-12-01`: the OpenSearch netty digest key CVE-2026-75595 on `opensearchproject/opensearch:3@sha256:bcc17975…` and three brotli CVE-2026-111497 digest keys on `caddy:2\.11\.7-alpine` and both postgres lines. The 2026-10-23 ca-certificates cohort has fully emptied: Keycloak cleared it by a same-version digest refresh (PR #838), mongo was discharged when upstream's UBI 9.8 rebuild of the same 9.0.4 shipped fixed ca-certificates, and the three langfuse entries (CVE-2026-114406 on web and worker, CVE-2026-114139 `@sentry/nextjs` on web) were discharged on 2026-11-01 (item #895) when both refs moved to `4.72.0`. Comment blocks describing absent entries (Keycloak 26.7.4, `langfuse:4`, the otel-lgtm amqp091-go trio, the `next` pair, the retired object store, the mongo 8.0.8 seed, the Unleash proxy-addr key, the langfuse 4.68.0 ca-certificates entries) are the file's history, not live suppressions.

The 2026-10-23 allowlist cohort is the file's normal shape — advisories published against images nobody changed: CVE-2026-114406 (base-image ca-certificates), the `next` GHSAs and CVE-2026-114139 (`@sentry/nextjs`) turned `infra-image-scan` red for every compose / `renovate.json` PR (#836, #837) although the pins were untouched. Whether the bump remediates is measured per image, and the cohort has now emptied, having produced all three endings. Entries were version-keyed to the pin the run actually scans (`langfuse/langfuse` and `langfuse/langfuse-worker` at `4\.68\.0`, re-keyed from 4.56.0 by spec 081 US8 PR 8d / item #839 on 2026-10-25 after a verify-RED run on the new digests) so that a bump re-blocked rather than inheriting the suppression, and each justification stated the entry is deleted once a clean rebuild ships. Keycloak cleared the same CVE by a same-version digest refresh in PR #838; the two `next` GHSAs were DELETED rather than re-keyed in the same change that moved langfuse to 4.68.0 (it ships next 16.4.2 and neither advisory appears at any severity, so a re-keyed entry would have matched nothing); `grafana/otel-lgtm` was discharged when the 2026-10-30 window moved it to `0.38.1@sha256:0df9bc14…730af7`, a clean rebuild reporting the CVE neither blocking nor allowlisted (PR #878); mongo was discharged when upstream's UBI 9.8 rebuild of the same 9.0.4 (`sha256:3d40c6fa895f`, the digest every mongo ref now pins) shipped the fixed ca-certificates 2026.2.92_v9.0.319-90.3.el9_8, scanned at zero fixable Criticals; and the three langfuse entries were DISCHARGED on 2026-11-01 (item #895), when both refs moved to `4.72.0` on a clean rebuild Trivy reports at zero fixable Criticals, so a re-keyed entry would have matched nothing.

The `mongodb/mongodb-community-server` hold is discharged and replaced by an approval gate, and the re-own wrapper is what made the move safe. A renovate.json `allowedVersions: <9` ceiling (added 2026-10-23, item #819) existed because mongod 9.0.4 refused this host's kernel (SERVER-121912) and 9.0 runs mongod as uid 1000 where 8.0.8 used 998, so it could not open an 8.0 volume. Spec 081 US8a (PR #817) discharged both premises: the host moved to a 7.0.0 patch that 9.0.4's Ubuntu exemption admits (SERVER-131779), every mongo ref moved to the digest-pinned `9.0-ubi9`, every MongoDB service mounting `/data/db` now starts as `0:0` only to re-own the volume and drops to the image's `mongod` user with `setpriv` before mongod runs, and the ceiling was lifted. The guard asserts the SUCCESSOR rather than the absence — no `allowedVersions` on patch, minor or major, `dependencyDashboardApproval` true on a major and undefined on a patch — because a `<9` left behind would block the deployed version and make Renovate propose a downgrade.

`scripts/__tests__/mongo-data-owner.guard.test.mjs` is the second lock on the MongoDB image move: it requires every service in the dev AND prod compose files that mounts `/data/db` to start as `0:0`, to use the `sh -c` wrapper with `$0` `mongo-data-owner`, and to run `mongod`, asserts the wrapper text is identical across all four files, executes the wrapper against stubs so the assertion is about what it does (re-own only when the data is foreign-owned, then drop to `mongod`; no chown and no setpriv when not root) rather than how it is spelled, and requires at least one matching service per file so a rename cannot make every assertion pass vacuously.

`scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` asserts each discharged stateful-datastore hold as its SUCCESSOR rather than as an absent ceiling — no `allowedVersions` on patch, minor or major plus a `dependencyDashboardApproval` major gate and an automatic patch stream for vault, opensearch, langfuse, the shared observability postgres and mongodb — because a hold deliberately discharged and one someone deleted are indistinguishable from the absence of a ceiling, and because a ceiling left behind would block the version actually deployed. The controls matter as much as the assertions: the vault and item #407 holds must not widen onto caddy, otel-lgtm, postgres, redis, keycloak or clickhouse, and the langfuse server and worker must still resolve identically on both keys because they are one deployment sharing one database.

An allowlist entry that suppresses nothing is DELETED in the change that discharges it rather than left to age out, because an unmatched entry keeps failing `--check-expiring` whatever its date — so spec 081 US8 PR 8d deleted the two `next` GHSAs (GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw / GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr) instead of re-keying them: langfuse 4.68.0 ships next 16.4.2 and neither advisory appears on either image at any severity, while a re-keyed entry would have matched nothing; the entries whose advisories the new pin still carries were re-keyed to `4\.68\.0` with the same expiry in the same change, and the gate passes with 0 unmatched entries afterwards.

The CVE-2026-111497 brotli cohort is the allowlist's only set keyed to the DIGEST ALONE with no version in the key, because the suppression must be discharged by a REBUILD rather than by a tag move: Renovate proposes from the registry rather than from this file, so every rebuild is still offered, the new digest is scanned unsuppressed, and the Renovate PR's own scan proves whether the rebuild carries the fixed brotli instead of inheriting the acceptance, while the old entry stops matching. It opened as six entries and is now THREE, all renewed to `2026-12-01` by the 2026-11-01 re-triage (Trivy 0.76.1, ghcr DB, every newest rebuild scanned): `^caddy:2\.11\.7-alpine@sha256:d8542f48d34a`, `^postgres:18-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32` and `^postgres:18\.6-alpine3\.23@sha256:697c180dbf24`, each renewed on MEASURED non-reachability recorded in its own justification rather than on the clock — in each of those digests the only object linking `libbrotlidec` is `libcurl.so.4.8.0` (for caddy its only consumer is the curl CLI, which that service never runs, since Caddy is a static Go binary and the healthcheck is `nc -z`; for postgres the only thing linking libcurl is the `libpq` OAuth-client module the server never loads, the only client run being `pg_isready` with no OAuth parameters) — and none of the three has a clean rebuild upstream (Alpine 3.24's brotli-libs 1.2.0-r1 is not the fix). The cohort's other three entries were deleted rather than renewed: `curlimages/curl` 8.23.0 and `httpd` 2.4 both moved to clean rebuilds, and `rustfs/rustfs` had already moved 1.0.3 → 1.0.4 so its key matched nothing.

The scan report is a gitignored artifact rather than a committed record: `security/infra-images/reports/*` is ignored except for a `.gitkeep`, and the CI job uploads that directory as the `infra-image-scan-report` artifact with a 14-day retention under an `always()`-guarded step on the scan path, so a red sweep still leaves its findings readable. `scripts/__tests__/upload-artifact-retention.test.mjs` pins that every `upload-artifact` step in every workflow sets a whole-number retention and that a diagnostics upload named `*scan*` stays at or under 14 days.

A digest-keyed allowlist entry whose digest moves becomes invisible rather than merely stale: unmatched detection is scoped to `generatedForImages` (item #423), so an entry whose image regex matches none of the images the run scanned is silent by design, while only the EXPIRING/EXPIRED tiers — computed over the whole allowlist — will ever surface it. The brotli cohort produced the measured case: the tree moved `rustfs/rustfs` to `1.0.4@sha256:ed9210d6…` on 2026-10-30, so the `^rustfs/rustfs:1\.0\.3@sha256:9ca9559533b5` key suppressed nothing and was never reported as UNMATCHED; the 2026-11-01 re-triage found it by reading the cohort and DELETED it rather than renewing it, which is why the recorded cue is to delete each such entry as its digest bump lands rather than renew it without re-scanning. The three surviving brotli keys still name today's pins, and their `2026-12-01` expiry windows are what will surface them if a rebuild lands first.

The shared per-image pipeline is what moved the deploy gate onto the pull request (spec 084 US3, item #822): app-ci's required `app-image-scan` job runs `scripts/cd/scan-app-image.sh` on the six images `app-e2e` already built, which `app-e2e` tags `app-scan/<name>:run-<run id>` so a later rebuild of `:latest` on the persistent daemon cannot change what is scanned, and holds with a labelled stopped container so another run's `docker image prune -af` cannot delete the tag. The job needs `[changes, app-e2e]` but is `always()`-guarded so a skipped `app-e2e` cannot skip it, runs on the `kvm` runner holding the images, passes early and explicitly when no app path changed, fails naming a missing scan tag rather than passing on images it could not find, scans every image even after one fails so one run names every blocking image, removes its holds and then the run-scoped tags under `always()`, and is required by `trigger-cd` so a red scan on `main` blocks the dispatch before any deploy.

`scripts/__tests__/app-image-scan.test.mjs` is the drift guard that keeps the PR and the deploy on one pipeline: it fails if either caller (`scripts/cd/scan-push.sh` or the `app-image-scan` job's steps) runs the scanner or the verdict itself instead of `scripts/cd/scan-app-image.sh`, requires both to scan exactly the six repositories `scan-push.sh`'s image map pushes and `app-e2e` to tag the same set, and pins the wiring — `app-ci / app-image-scan*` in `ci-status`'s `REQUIRED_CONTEXT_GLOBS` and `scripts/cd/scan-app-image.sh` in app-ci's `app` path filter, so a change to the shared scan triggers the job that runs it.

The `generatedForImages` scoping check tolerates a report that is explicitly marked absent (`reportAbsent: true` — the marker the gate's own ENOENT path sets under `--check-expiring`) by returning an empty result set, which is what stopped the weekly allowlist-expiry step crashing on a report no scan had produced; the exemption is keyed on that explicit marker and never on the field merely being missing, so a report that EXISTS and omits `generatedForImages` is still a hard `GateError` and a producer that stops writing the field fails rather than silently restoring all-in-scope unmatched detection.

A dated allowlist cohort is re-triaged in one sitting, and the re-triage is where a stale key is actually found rather than at its expiry date. The 2026-11-01 sitting (Trivy 0.76.1, ghcr DB, every newest rebuild scanned) is the shape to copy: each entry in the cohort is re-measured against the newest upstream build before any date is renewed, a clean rebuild deletes the entry and moves the ref, a tag that has already moved deletes the entry because it can no longer match, and an entry with no clean rebuild is renewed with its non-reachability re-measured and recorded in its own justification — because renewing a suppression without a fresh scan is exactly the thing the time-box exists to prevent.

app-ci's `app-image-scan` job fails closed when the `changes` job did not succeed, because whether the app images changed is then unknown and an unknown diff must not read as "nothing to scan"; the early pass is reserved for the measured case where `needs.changes.outputs.app` is not `true`. Past that decision the job verifies all six run-scoped scan tags with `docker image inspect` before scanning anything and fails naming every missing one, and each image then runs in its own step under `always() && RUN_SCAN == 'true' && SCAN_READY == 'true'` so one failing scan does not stop the rest and a single run names every blocking image.

The PR-time scan's run-scoped tags are protected from the shared runner's prunes by a labelled stopped container rather than by a lock (item #915, research R15): the single `kvm` runner can take another run's `app-e2e`, `dast` or `build-deploy` between this run's `app-e2e` and its `app-image-scan`, and each of those starts with `docker image prune -af`, which deletes a bare tag (PR #909 failed `missing scan tag(s)` twice that way). Because `image prune -a` never removes an image that has a container, the tag step creates `app-scan-hold-<run id>-<name>` labelled `mcm.app-scan-hold=run-<run id>` on the run-scoped tag after a `docker rm -f` (a re-run attempt keeps the run id), and each of the three image-prune sites first sweeps only stale holds with `docker container prune -f --filter label=mcm.app-scan-hold --filter until=24h`, so a cancelled run's images are released within a day while a run still awaiting its scan keeps them. `scripts/__tests__/app-image-scan.test.mjs` pins the sweep-before-prune ordering, the label and age filters, the hold-before-tag removal, the count of prune sites, and the absence of any unfiltered `docker system prune` / `docker container prune`.

`scripts/ci-install-trivy.sh <vX.Y.Z> <bindir>` is the ONE Trivy installer all three scanning workflows call, so the PR gates and the deploy scan cannot drift on the scanner. It downloads the release tarball and its checksums file directly from GitHub release assets, verifies the sha256 (requiring exactly one checksums entry for the asset), and refuses to finish unless the installed binary reports the pinned version — so a passing install step means *this* version is on PATH, not that a version line was printed. It replaced Trivy's own `contrib/install.sh`, which was fetched from a moving branch and piped into `sh` and, on PR #929 (runs 6696 and 6702, 2026-11-04), failed twice with no error at all because it fetches the tarball from `get.trivy.dev`, logs a non-200 at DEBUG level, and `set -e` turns that into a silent exit.

`scripts/__tests__/ci-install-trivy.test.mjs` pins the installer's own behaviour offline against `file://` fixtures: a good release installs the pinned version into `<bindir>` with the checksum verified, a checksum mismatch fails loudly and installs nothing usable, a failed download names the URL and curl's exit rather than exiting silently (the PR #929 failure), a binary reporting a different version fails so a green step means the PINNED version, and a tag that is not `vX.Y.Z` is refused before anything is fetched.
